Deals no damage and grants no attack advantage by itself.
Drag at half speed; target may use its action for a contested escape; release freely.
Shove or Takedown requires a separate attack and contest.
Pushing the target away normally ends the grapple.

powers.rules_status: Level, cost, radius, and damage confirmed; save, self-exclusion, success result, and prone rider are adopted table rulings.

opening_crawl.cinematic_exposition:
The Meridian Reach had learned long ago not to wait for rescue.

Its settlements were scattered across wide distances, joined by old trade lanes, volunteer relays, and the stubborn belief that a neighbor in need should never have to ask twice. The Republic had brought law and learning to the frontier, but it was the people of the Reach who kept its farms alive, its ships moving, and its isolated worlds speaking to one another through the dark.

The Jedi who came here had understood that.

They did not arrive as generals or judges. They walked the fields, repaired moisture pumps, listened to old grievances, and slept beneath the same leaking roofs as the people they served. In time, the frontier gave them a name of its own.

The Walking Cloaks.

Aeleron Do'ordo had grown beneath the shadow of that tradition.

Now, for the first time, no master stood beside him.

Vael Taron had disappeared somewhere within the Reach, leaving behind no body, no final message, and no answer beyond the faint impression Aero had felt after four days of meditation: distant, obscured, but not gone.

The Council had given Aero a title.

Knight.

The word still felt heavier than the lightsaber at his side.

His first command was supposed to be simple.

A Republic shuttle carried him toward the outer reaches of the sector with three young operatives he had never met before and six engineers whose equipment crates filled most of the aft compartment. Their destination was an abandoned beacon relay — one of the old frontier links that had gone silent after years of neglect.

Restore the station. Confirm the signal. Bring everyone home.

Routine work.

The kind of work the Walking Cloaks had once done without ceremony.

Beyond the viewport, the stars stretched across the black, and somewhere ahead of them the Meridian Reach waited — quiet, familiar, and still holding the last trace of Aero's missing master.

---

The shuttle's cabin hums with recycled air and the low harmonics of the hyperdrive. Dax Ferren fills the cockpit doorway with one boot on the frame, halfway through a story nobody asked for. Besk Ollor's six engineers have colonized the aft compartment, their crates strapped in tight rows. And across the cabin sit the three operatives the Republic assigned to Aero's first command — Senn Varga checking his gear for the fourth time, Ilo Reeth watching the young Knight without quite watching him, Maza Ketrel counting ration packs against a manifest.

None of them have served together before. All of them know who his master was.

entries.text: I say: "Hello."

entries.narration: The shuttle's interior hums with the low thrum of engines and the occasional rattle from its cargo hold. Beside you, Chief Engineer Besk Ollor is hunched over a schematic table, his gruff demeanor not quite masking a hint of concern.
entries.behavior: Besk leans back slightly, tapping a stylus against the edge of the table, his eyes flicking between you and the schematics intermittently.

entries.text: You’re new to this, aren’t you? But I’ve seen a lot of young Jedi — and you look like someone who’s ready for the worst.
entries.behavior: Besk straightens up slightly, his eyes holding yours in a challenge-like gaze.

entries.text: I look him up and down and say "What do you classify as the worst?" my face does not change from its previous state.
The worst is when you're out here alone with a malfunctioning crate and no hope of rescue.
entries.behavior: leans back in his chair, sighs deeply

entries.text: "Ah, so just one malfunctioning crate can end the job? What are all the other crates for?" I ask almost challenging his competence.
Those crates are for hardware and parts necessary to reactivate the sensor array. If any of those fail, it could jeopardize the entire mission.
entries.behavior: Ilo crosses his arms, looking at Aero with a steady gaze.

entries.text: Yeah. I need those parts to be in perfect condition. And don't even think about touching them, Jedi.
entries.behavior: Besk leans back and glares at Aero from across the schematics table.

entries.text: I head to the back to look at the crates. I put 1 finger on them as I sweep them visually for any defects.

entries.narration: You move to the aft cargo bay where six crates are stacked neatly. The labels indicate they contain crucial hardware and parts for reactivating the sensor array. You run your finger along the edges, checking for any signs of damage or tampering.
entries.behavior: You place a single finger on each crate as you visually inspect them.

entries.text: Hey, what do you think you're doing with those crates?
entries.narration: Besk Ollor, the chief engineer, appears from his seat, clearly concerned by your inspection.
entries.behavior: Besk steps between you and the crates, his posture defensive.

entries.text: "Interesting." I say, unamused. My face the same expression as when I said hello and he challenged my gaze. "If you're here, then who is looking at the same schematics you have been trying to figure out since we got on the ship. I'm no engineer, I wouldn't claim to know what they're supposed to mean before I started the mission. You on the other hand...." my voice trails off condescendingly. I reach out with the force to get a gauge on his intent.
No legal power supports this effect. Known powers: Battle Insight, Burst. The Force does not answer — narrate the attempt failing or falling short.

entries.narration: Aeleron's condescending tone hangs in the air, and Besk Ollor's gruff demeanor flares. The tension between you is palpable as he glances at the schematics, then back to you.
entries.behavior: Besk folds his arms and leans slightly forward, his eyes narrowing.

entries.text: "I've been working on these schematics since we boarded. Every detail matters to me, Jedi. One mistake and the entire mission could be jeopardized. So, I'll ask again: what are you doing with those crates?"
entries.behavior: Besk points towards the aft cargo bay where the crates are stored.

entries.text: "How about you go sit in your chair like a good boy and do the job you should have done 2 weeks ago in preparation for this mission. Ilo, any objections with Mr. Ollor doing his job?" I scan his body language for any sign of movement or attacking.
I need you to stay out of my way, Jedi. These crates are delicate and require precise handling.
entries.behavior: Besk crosses his arms, his eyes narrowing as he watches Aero.

entries.text: Actually, Besk, maybe you should listen to the Jedi. He's here for a reason.
entries.behavior: Ilo raises an eyebrow at Besk and then glances at Aero, her tone calm but firm.

entries.narration: Besk's gaze flicks to Ilo, and his expression softens slightly, but he still looks wary.

entries.text: "I'm here to ensure the mission's success, Besk. If you have concerns, let's address them together."
Fine, Jedi. But if anything goes wrong with these crates, I'll be pointing fingers at you.
entries.behavior: Besk crosses his arms and glares at Aero.

entries.text: Let's not start off on the wrong foot. We're all here to do a job, right?
entries.behavior: Ilo stands between Besk and Aero, trying to ease the tension.

entries.text: I move towards Besk with my hand out looking to shake hands and move past it. I say: "You did well, you could've been a jedi in another life." with my hand still out to see if he accepts.

entries.narration: Besk looks at your outstretched hand with a mix of suspicion and mild amusement. He considers it for a moment before finally reaching out to shake your hand.
entries.behavior: Besk reaches his hand towards yours, but keeps his posture tense.

entries.text: "You did well, you could've been a jedi in another life." Fine, Jedi. Let's just get this mission done without any hitches.
entries.behavior: Besk shakes your hand firmly but quickly lets go to maintain his distance.

entries.text: "Before we proceed, let's quickly review the key points of our plan. I want to make sure everyone is on the same page."

entries.narration: Besk Ollor looks at you with a gruff expression, but he extends his hand in return and firmly shakes yours.
entries.behavior: Besk reaches out and shakes your hand, his grip firm yet cautious.

entries.text: Good to see some camaraderie forming here. We should definitely go over the plan again before we land.
entries.behavior: Senn Varga stands up from his seat, looking earnestly at you.

entries.text: I agree. It’s been a while since I’ve reviewed the schematics. We should all be on the same page.
entries.behavior: Ilo Reeth nods, adjusting his glasses as he looks around the room.

entries.text: "Ilo are you male or female?" - **adjusting his glasses as he looks around the room. | Ilo raises an eyebrow at Besk and then glances at Aero, her tone calm but firm."

entries.narration: The shuttle's interior is filled with the hum of its engines and the occasional chatter from the crew. Besk Ollor sits across the schematics table, his posture tense but less hostile than before.

entries.text: I'm female, Aero. And I don't mind a quick review of the plan before we land. It's always good to be prepared.
entries.behavior: Ilo raises an eyebrow at Besk and then glances at Aero, her tone calm but firm.

entries.text: "Senn Varga, nice to make your acquaintance. What is your role on this mission?" I ask tone smooth but curious
Nice to meet you too, Aero. I’m Senn Varga, Republic field operative here for survey and security tasks. How about you?
entries.behavior: extends a hand in greeting, standing slightly at attention

entries.text: Senn’s role is clear, but I suppose it wouldn’t hurt to review our plan one more time. Besk, could you go over the essentials of reactivating the sensor array?
entries.behavior: adjusts glasses and looks at Besk expectantly

entries.text: I shake Senn's hand excitedly. I say "Pleasure to meet you. Clearly, Ilo is excited about reviewing these plans." I wink.
Good to meet you too, Aero. Let's get this mission squared away.
entries.behavior: Senn gives a slight nod and steps back towards the schematics table.

entries.text: Alright, let's go over this one last time. First things first: the sensor array has been offline for too long. We'll need to reset the power conduits and recalibrate the core units.
entries.behavior: Besk points at a section of the schematics spread out on the table.

entries.text: And don't forget about securing the comms. We'll need to ensure that our transmissions aren't being intercepted.
entries.behavior: Ilo glances at Aero with a mix of skepticism and professionalism, her eyes scanning over the schematics.
